{{Quote|The Queen and I&mdash;well, we've always talked of adopting a girl. If you have no objection, I would like to take Leia to Alderaan, and raise her as our daughter. She would be loved with us.|Bail Organa|<ref name="Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (novelization)">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]]</ref>}}
'''Breha Organa''', born '''Breha Antilles''', was a [[Gender/Legends|female]] [[Human/Legends|Human]] who was the [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] and [[Minister of Education/Legends|Minister of Education]] of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]] at the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire's]] [[Declaration of a New Order|formation]]. She was the [[Marriage/Legends|wife]] of [[Prince/Legends|Prince]] [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Organa]], [[Viceroy/Legends|Viceroy]] and [[First Chairman/Legends|First Chairman]] of the [[Alderaan system/Legends|Alderaan system]]. The couple longed for a [[Youngling/Legends|child]] for many [[Standard year/Legends|years]], but Queen Breha suffered multiple [[Reproduction|miscarriages]] that put her own life at risk. Eventually, the Organas adopted the baby girl of the late [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Amidala]] after the end of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. The couple raised the girl as their own daughter, the Princess [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]]. In the early [[Standard day/Legends|days]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], the Queen's family helped to build a [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|rebellion]] against that authoritarian dictatorship. Breha Organa later [[Death/Legends|perished]] when [[Destruction of Alderaan/Legends|the Empire destroyed Alderaan]] by blowing it up and turned the planet into an asteroid field with the [[Superlaser/Legends|superlaser]] of the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]] [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]]. Years after her passing, she was remembered as a loving mother, and a simple mention of her would still awaken a sense of patriotism in the surviving [[Alderaanian/Legends|Alderaanians]].

==Biography==
===Early life===
{{Quote|They grew up together. They're more like brother and sister.|Bail Organa, about Breha and her cousin|<ref name="CWWS">''[[The Clone Wars: Wild Space]]''</ref>}}
Breha Antilles was [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] on [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]], one of the [[Core Founder/Legends|founding]] [[Planet/Legends|planets]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]<ref name="SWCP" /> at some point between [[59 BBY/Legends|59 BBY]] and [[49 BBY/Legends|49 BBY]],<ref name="Birth" /> under the [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|chancellorship]] of either [[Thoris Darus]] or [[Frix]].<ref name="SWDP">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref> A [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|female]] of [[Noble/Legends|noble]] lineage, she was a member of the [[House of Antilles]], one of Alderaan's most influential families.<ref name="SWCP" /> She had at least one sister, [[Deara Antilles]], who looked much like her, although with a round face and a taller stature.<ref name="LotJ:MoD" /> She had a [[Breha Organa's cousin|cousin]], with whom she grew up and whom she considered a brother.<ref name="CWWS" /> She was also related to both [[Prince/Legends|Prince]] [[Bail Antilles/Legends|Bail Antilles]]<ref name="CSWEhoa">{{CSWECite|II|63|House of Antilles}}</ref> and [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Raymus Antilles/Legends|Raymus Antilles]], who was later entrusted with piloting the private [[Starship/Legends|vessel]] of the [[House of Organa/Legends|House of Organa]],<ref name="ROSV">''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> the [[Sundered Heart/Legends|''Sundered Heart'']].<ref name="SWB:RE">''[[Star Wars Blueprints: Rebel Edition]]''</ref>

===Queen of Alderaan===
{{Quote|Don't worry, B, nothing's wrong. I just wanted you to know I'm thinking of you. I was watching the HoloNet feed from the Senate. You look tired. Are you getting enough sleep? I'll bet you're not. Go to bed, hotshot. I'll try to catch you tomorrow.|Breha Organa, in a [[Hologram/Legends|hologram]] message to her husband Bail during the Clone Wars|<ref name="CWWS" />}}
[[File:Bail_Organa-FactFile.png|thumb|left|150px|Viceroy Bail Organa, the husband of Queen Breha]]
After the [[Alderaan Ascendancy Contention]], Breha [[Marriage/Legends|married]] [[Prince/Legends|Prince]] [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Prestor Organa]], and she took the mantle of [[King/Legends|Queen]] of Alderaan at some point before [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]]. During Queen Breha's wedding, the famous [[Alderaanian/Legends|Alderaanian]] [[Scientist/Legends|scientist]] [[Tryn Netzl]] acted as her groom's witness.<ref name="CWGSi">''[[Clone Wars Gambit: Siege]]''</ref> Breha Organa also enlisted her sister, making her a royal advisor.<ref name="LotJ:MoD" /> Beyond her royal role, Queen Breha also served as her planet's [[Minister of Education/Legends|Minister of Education]].<ref name="SWCP" />

Following the [[Supreme Chancellor election, 32 BBY/Legends|election]] of [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] as Supreme Chancellor of the Republic<ref name="dbAnt">{{DB|character|bailantilles|Antilles, Bail}}</ref> in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]],<ref name="NEC" /> Bail Organa acted as Senator of the [[Alderaan sector/Legends|Alderaan sector]] to the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]]. With her husband&mdash;whom she affectionately called "B"&mdash;serving on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]],<ref name="CWWS" /> Queen Breha often spent [[Standard day/Legends|days]] alone in her [[Royal Palace of Alderaan/Legends|palace]] in the [[Mountain/Legends|mountains]] over the [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of [[Aldera/Legends|Aldera]]. An influential and busy man, Senator Organa could rarely afford long trips to his home planet. Over the same period, Breha Organa befriended [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], Senator and former [[Monarch of Naboo/Legends|Queen]] of the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] planet [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]].<ref name="CWGSt">''[[Clone Wars Gambit: Stealth]]''</ref> The two women had many things in common, having both ruled their respective [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworlds]],<ref name="Revenge of the Sith" /><ref name="TPM">{{Film|I}}</ref> both of which were peaceful planets with pristine landscapes and a focus on art and philosophy.<ref name="TPMV">''[[Star Wars: Episode I: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref><ref name="C&CW">''[[Coruscant and the Core Worlds]]''</ref> When the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] broke out in 22 BBY, Bail Organa became even more engaged in the ongoing [[Politics/Legends|political]] turmoil, and Breha would only receive lightning visits from him.<ref name="CWGSt" />

Over the [[Standard year/Legends|years]], Breha and her husband had many difficulties in [[Reproduction/Legends|producing]] a [[Youngling/Legends|child]] and heir. The Queen had suffered at least five [[Reproduction|miscarriages]], despite receiving treatment from the best fertility [[Doctor/Legends|doctors]] in the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="CWGSi" /> After the last miscarriage in [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]], her doctors informed her that another attempt to conceive would probably [[Death/Legends|kill]] her.<ref name="R61">[[Republic 61|''Republic'' 61]]</ref> The Queen's husband suffered tremendously as a result of the repeated mournings, and he often attempted to drown his sorrows in [[Alcohol/Legends|alcohol]] under the benevolent surveillance of his friend Tryn Netzl.<ref name="CWGSi" />

That same year, the Queen's brotherly cousin, who served as a [[Tactical officer/Legends|tactical officer]] in the [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]], was killed in the destruction of his ship ''[[Bespin Dancer]]'' during a [[Fall of Falleen|battle]] over [[Falleen/Legends|Falleen]]. Arguing that his wife should be informed by him personally and not by an impersonal communiqué, Bail Organa broke protocol and told Queen Breha about the demise of her kinsman. Upon hearing the news, the Queen of Alderaan reacted with deep, if muted, sorrow.<ref name="CWWS" />

===Adopting the young Leia===
{{Quote|No happier fate could any child ask for. With our blessing, and that of the Force, let Leia be your child.|Yoda to Bail Organa|<ref name="Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (novelization)" />}}
[[File:BailBrehaLeia-hd.png|thumb|250px|Breha holding her newly adopted daughter Leia]]
In [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], the fury of the Clone Wars ended. The three-year long conflict had left very deep wounds all over [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], but the hardest part was yet to come. Chancellor Palpatine, who was in fact a powerful [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] known as [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Sidious, dismantled the Republic and replaced it with his despotic [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. The Senator Amidala, who had been Queen Breha's friend, was among the indirect fatalities of the regime change, leaving behind her newborn [[Twin/Legends|twins]]: a boy named [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke]] and a girl named [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia]]. In reality, those children had been fathered by [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], a famed Jedi Knight who had turned to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]]. Unbeknownst to most people in the [[galactic community]], Skywalker became the right-hand man of the Emperor Palpatine, wearing the name and [[Darth Vader's armor/Legends|heavy armor]] of Darth Vader.<ref name="Revenge of the Sith" />

With the blessing and sanction of the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]], Queen Breha Organa and her husband then took Leia in, committed to loving her as their own child. Through adoption, Amidala's baby girl became Leia Organa, Princess of Alderaan.<ref name="Revenge of the Sith" /> Soon thereafter, when Bail's former [[senatorial aide]] [[Sheltay Retrac/Legends|Sheltay Retrac]] and her [[Sheltay Retrac's husband|husband]] died, Breha and Bail also adopted their orphaned daughter, the infant [[Winter Celchu|Winter]].<ref name="SWCP" /> The couple raised both girls together, although Winter was not considered royalty.<ref name="RD">''[[Rebel Dawn]]''</ref> A third foster child, the young [[Neena]], was also raised in the Organa household.<ref name="GG6">[[Galaxy Guide 6: Tramp Freighters (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 6: Tramp Freighters'', Second Edition]]</ref> The new parents relied on Prince Bail's sisters [[Rouge Organa|Rouge]], [[Tia Organa|Tia]], and [[Celly Organa/Legends|Celly Organa]] to assist them in their parental work.<ref name="Databank">{{DB|character|bailorgana|Organa, Bail}}</ref>

Despite her heavy responsibilities and status, Queen Breha was extensively involved in taking care of Leia,<ref name="LotJ:MoD" /> nicknamed Lelila,<ref name="CS">''[[The Crystal Star]]''</ref> during the princess' infancy. She took time to enjoy small things with her daughter, such as picking [[Plant/Legends|flowers]] and running through the castle's [[Grass/Legends|grassy]] gardens. However, with the Galactic Empire [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|hunting down]] the remaining Jedi Knights, Breha and Bail Organa feared that Leia's [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitivity]] could be discovered, which urged them to remain on their guard. Notwithstanding the royal couple's best efforts, a very close relative eventually betrayed their trust and confidence. In [[18 BBY/Legends|18 BBY]], Breha found out that her own sister Deara Antilles had been working as a spy for Darth Vader himself. Worse still, Antilles had sought to expose Leia's Forceful reflexes to the agents of the Empire. Such a [[Treason/Legends|treason]] broke Breha Organa's heart, but she retained her trademark dignity when she confronted the culprit. For the sake of sisterly love, the Queen refused to put Deara in [[Prison/Legends|jail]], arranging a secret passage for her and a safehouse on the remote planet [[Ankori-7]].<ref name="LotJ:MoD" />

During Leia and Winter's childhood, the Queen of Alderaan continued to organize formal receptions at the Palace, during which the lady guests used to wear formal yet elegant dresses. On the occasion of Princess Leia's twelfth [[Birthday/Legends|birthday]], Breha Organa was noted for wearing a tasteful red [[Silk/Legends|silk]] gown. More than a decade later, Winter&mdash;who had developed a eidetic memory&mdash;would remember that particular celebration with extreme precision.<ref name="Scoundrels">''[[Scoundrels]]''</ref> On at least one occasion, the princess went over the wall while her parents were tight asleep. However, two members of the Alderaan Guard found her at a party and escorted her back to the palace. Both the Viceroy and the Queen were awaiting their daughter on the doorstep, looking obviously discontented.<ref name="Swac">''[[Star Wars Art: Comics]]''</ref> In the meantime, far from the pomp and protocol of the Court, the whole House of Organa operated in secret against Palpatine's Empire. The Queen's husband Bail Organa eventually became one of the founders of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]], better known as the "Rebel Alliance."<ref name="TFUG">''[[The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

===Death and legacy===
{{Quote|It was night in our palace&mdash;were you awake or asleep, with Mother&hellip; or alone?|Leia Organa|<ref name="LGFA" />}}
[[File:Breha_and_Bail_death.png|thumb|left|200px|Queen Breha and Viceroy Organa's last moments]]
In [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]],<ref name="NEC" /> the Empire chose to get rid of Alderaan as an example. With the help of the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]], a [[Moon/Legends|moon]]-sized [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] that could deliver a considerable amount of firepower, the Imperial [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Tarkin]] blew up the peaceful planet.<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref> On a warm evening late in the spring,<ref name="CotJ">[[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']]</ref> Breha Organa died in the [[Destruction of Alderaan/Legends|destruction]] of her world, along with her husband and millions of her loyal subjects.<ref name="Topps">{{Topps|set=2013 Topps Star Wars Illustrated: A New Hope|cardname=The Destruction of Alderaan}}</ref> A few years later, the still-grieving Leia Organa wondered whether her adopted parents were spending the night together or each on their own when the Death Star's planet-killing [[Superlaser/Legends|superlaser]] struck.<ref name="LGFA" /> In truth, Bail and Breha Organa had indeed been awake when the blast hit Alderaan, spending their last moments together in a close embrace.<ref name="Topps" />

[[File:Leia_NEC.jpg|thumb|150px|Princess Leia, the Queen's heiress]]
A few months after the cataclysm, the orphaned princess used her mother's given name as an alias while dealing with [[Tag Rogaren]], a former chief weapon systems engineer of the Empire who had taken refuge in a battered [[Venator-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Venator''-class Star Destroyer]]. However, being an Alderaanian himself, Rogaren saw through the Princess' lie, and he admitted having worked on the Death Star's superlaser.<ref name="SW09">[[Star Wars (2013) 9|''Star Wars'' (2013) 9]]</ref> [[4 ABY/Legends|Four years later]],<ref name="NEC" /> when Leia Organa discovered the forests of [[Endor/Legends|Endor]], the gargantuan [[Tree/Legends|trees]] reminded her of those "giants" among whom she had lived on Alderaan, including her mother Breha.<ref name="ROJN">[[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode VI: Return of the Jedi'' novel]]</ref> Around [[5 ABY/Legends|5 ABY]], Leia Organa once evoked the authority of the late queen to convince the Alderaanian [[Tycho Celchu/Legends|Tycho Celchu]] to let her fly with him in a [[A/SF-01 B-wing starfighter/Legends|B-wing]] [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]]. While the Princess hated trading on her dead family's station, she knew that the memory of Breha could appeal to patriotic sentiments and help her achieve her aims.<ref name="LSSM">''[[Luke Skywalker and the Shadows of Mindor]]''</ref>

Following their reunion as brother and sister, Princess Leia and Luke Skywalker tried to discover the identity of their true mother. They often sat in a Jedi [[Meditation/Legends|meditation]] circle, calling on the [[Force ghost/Legends|spirits]] of those who might have known her. Among other persons, the twins tried to contact Bail and Breha Organa, but the spirits of Leia's foster parents did not answer their call&mdash;which Skywalker considered "a conspiracy of silence."<ref name="BtS">''[[Before the Storm]]''</ref> In [[29 ABY/Legends|29 ABY]],<ref name="TERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''</ref> Leia Organa acquired the painting entitled ''[[Killik Twilight]]'', which had once hung outside her bedroom in House Organa on Alderaan. That [[Moss painting/Legends|moss painting]] was the last existing emotional link to her childhood with her adoptive parents.<ref name="TUF">''[[The New Jedi Order: The Unifying Force]]''</ref>

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|How dare you say that! My husband's courage fills my heart with pride. He does not bring danger to this house. He brings honor to it. You are the one who brought dishonor and danger here.|Queen Breha to her sister Deara Antilles|<ref name="LotJ:MoD" />}}
[[File:Leia-ROTScomic.png|thumb|left|200px|Queen Breha, Bail Organa and their foster daughter]]
Breha Organa was a light-skinned woman with [[Color/Legends|brown]] [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] and black [[Hair/Legends|hair]] that she kept long,<ref name="SWCP" /> as was customary among Alderaanian adults.<ref name="CS" /> One of her royal outfits she wore around 19 BBY consisted of a blue metallic brocade gown with slit sleeves. When wearing that dress, she would braid a [[Gold/Legends|golden]] fabric into her hair, wrap it around her head, with the whole hairstyle covered by a blue semi-transparent veil. That silk-like shawl had two long tails in front descending to above the knees and one tail reaching above the robe's hem, and was decorated with gray leaf patterns. The gown's collar was adorned with a gold buckle-like brooch.<ref name="DAG">''[[Dressing a Galaxy: The Costumes of Star Wars]]''</ref> She was faithful to that style of dress, which she still wore around the time of her death.<ref name="Topps" />

Despite her husband's extended absences, Breha Organa did not hold that against him. Much to the contrary, the Queen was understanding and caring, making enquiries about Bail Organa's whereabouts and health.<ref name="CWWS" /> When she was in her midthirties, she stood out as a trustworthy, peaceful woman.<ref name="AoSW3">''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode III: Revenge of the Sith]]''</ref> She was also able to maintain regal composure even in the most terrible situations of suffering. When her sister Deara was exposed as a spy, Queen Breha remained calm and rational even though her husband exhibited clear signs of anger. However, Breha Organa would not renege her blood ties, and she refused to have her sister executed or imprisoned despite the seriousness of her offence.<ref name="LotJ:MoD" />

In private, the Queen and the Viceroy were still enamored of each other after years of marriage. Breha had a musical laugh that her husband considered sultry.<ref name="CWGSt" /> She would call him "B" or "hotshot", and he would nickname her "my dove."<ref name="CWWS" /> During the dark times that followed the rise of the Empire, Breha Organa felt immensely proud of her husband because of his courageous actions against Palpatine's regime.<ref name="LotJ:MoD" /> As a child, Leia Organa perceived how intensely her adopted parents were attached to each other, and she later described them as "very much in love."<ref name="ALL">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Allies]]''</ref> A lover of the finer things, the Queen maintained a collection of [[Braaken glass/Legends|braaken glass]], which her husband and daughter found hideous.<ref name="SOL">''[[Shield of Lies]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
===Character origins===
[[File:Leonore_Organa.png|thumb|right|150px|Concept art of Queen Organa by Iain McCaig, in the likeness of his wife]]
{{Quote|I thought that Queen Organa might look almost exacly like Padmé, because Leia remembers seeing her mother smile.|Iain McCaig|<ref name="AoSW3" />}}
The origin of the name "Queen Breha" can be traced back to the [[1974]] [[The Star Wars rough draft|rough draft]] of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'']], as the name given to the mother of the fourteen-year-old Princess Leia, and wife of [[King/Legends|King]] [[Kayos]] of [[Aquilae (The Star Wars)|Aquilae]].<ref name="DB-Solo, Princess Leia Organa">{{DB|character|leiaorganasolo|Solo, Princess Leia Organa}}</ref><ref name="The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film">''[[The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film]]''</ref> In this 132-page early story treatment, Breha was described as "a warm, silver-haired matron."<ref name="roughdraft">{{WebCite|url=http://www.starwarz.com/starkiller/the-star-wars-rough-draft|text=THE STAR WARS by George Lucas - Rough Draft|work=Starkiller - The Jedi Bendu Script Site|archivedate=20191219100824}}</ref> That first version of Queen Breha appears in the comic book series ''[[The Star Wars]]'', a [[Canon|non-canon]] adaptation of George Lucas's 1974 draft for ''Star Wars''. In that comic, the design of [[Breha (The Star Wars)|Queen Breha]] resembles<ref name="TSWpreview">''[[The Star Wars]]'' {{C|May the 4th special digital preview}}</ref> a [[:File:Scary Lira.png|concept drawing]] of Princess Leia in [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]], originally drawn by [[Ralph McQuarrie]] for [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']],<ref name="The Art of Star Wars Episode V: The Empire Strikes Back">''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode V: The Empire Strikes Back]]''</ref> and that was ultimately reused to portray [[Lira Wessex/Legends|Lira Wessex]] in the adventure book ''[[Crisis on Cloud City (adventure book)|Crisis on Cloud City]]''.<ref name="Crisis">[[Crisis on Cloud City (adventure book)|''Crisis on Cloud City'']]</ref>

In [[December]] [[2002]], George Lucas informed his production staff that "Queen Organa" would appear in [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']], the third installment of the ''Star Wars'' [[prequel trilogy]], which was in early pre&ndash;production at the time. Lucas described her as a peaceful, trustworthy woman in her midthirties. Based on those elements, illustrator [[Iain McCaig]] drew at least three conceptual artworks of the Queen. In one of them, McCaig sought to capture the spirit of his wife Leonor. In another drawing, he gave the Queen the traits of Padmé Amidala, in order to explain how Leia Organa could remember seeing the smile of her mother.<ref name="AoSW3" />

===Portrayal===
[[File:MendozaBTS.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Rebecca Jackson Mendoza during a fitting seance with Trisha Biggar]]
{{Quote|As a girl growing up and seeing ''Star Wars'', of course you want to be Princess Leia. And to know that I'm actually playing her mother&hellip; I just kept thinking about those buns! I was the mother of those buns! Maybe I taught her how to do those buns!|Rebecca Jackson Mendoza, on playing Breha Organa|<ref name="Beacon">{{HBCite|161}}</ref>}}
In [[2005]], Breha Organa made her first in-the-flesh appearance with the release of ''Star Wars Episode III: Revenge of the Sith'', in which she was portrayed by the [[Wikipedia:Australia|Australian]] actress and singer [[Rebecca Jackson Mendoza]].<ref name="Revenge of the Sith" /> Although a fan of the [[original trilogy]], Jackson Mendoza did not immediately understand the implications of playing "the Queen of Alderaan" in the last ''Star Wars'' movie. When her brothers helped her realize she would be the surrogate mother of Leia Organa, her excitement grew. Watching the trilogy as a young girl, Rebecca Jackson Mendoza had wished she could be Princess Leia, and playing her foster mother was something of an accomplishment.<ref name="Beacon" />

Queen Breha's only robe in the movie,<ref name="Beacon" /> which was referred to as "Alderaan Palace Dress" in ''[[Dressing a Galaxy: The Costumes of Star Wars]]'',<ref name="DAG" /> was created by [[Trisha Biggar]], who worked as costume designer for all three prequel films. It originally consisted of a green velvet garment that Jackson Mendoza compared to a "wedding gown," but the fabric was changed so that it would not look too dark on screen.<ref name="Beacon" />

===Character development and discrepancies===
{{Quote|By contrast, but similar to many other Star Wars kids, Leia was raised by a single parent. Her father was Bail Organa, Viceroy of the planet Alderaan and driving force of the Rebel Alliance.|Extract from "The Kids of Star Wars"|<ref name="SWK">{{SWArchive|url=kids/explore/lore/news20020729.html|text=The Kids of ''Star Wars''}}</ref>}}
The adopted mother of Princess Leia Organa was first mentioned in the [[1981]] [[Star Wars (1977) 53|''The Last Gift From Alderaan!'']], the fifty-third issue of the ''Star Wars'' comic book series by [[Marvel Comics]]. In this story, Princess Leia wondered whether her father was alone or "with Mother" when their home planet was destroyed by the Empire.<ref name="LGFA" /> Two years [[1983|later]], the Princess' foster mother was also alluded to in [[James Kahn]]'s [[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|novelization]] of [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']], as "[Leia's] mother, then Minister of Education."<ref name="ROJN" />

[[File:Dreaming_of_Mother.png|thumb|200px|A young Princess Leia musing on the absence of a mother in her life]]
However, the idea of Leia's surrogate mother living up to the destruction of Alderaan was ignored by most post-1983 sources. The Marvel comic series being considered "Secondary Canon," its content was made available to be used or discarded as needed by later authors.<ref name="FBChee">{{Facebook|noprofile=1|url=notes/keeper-of-the-holocron/whatd-i-say-again-select-posts-by-me-regarding-continuity/201910849829849|name=[[Leland Chee]]|date=2011-04-06|quote=There is a secondary "S" continuity classification used for older published materials created when there was less attention to making everything in the EU fit with everything else in the EU.|nobackup=1}}</ref> The [[1995]] novel [[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']] by Barbara Hambly stated that Leia Organa had been raised by her paternal aunts,<ref name="CotJ" /> an information that was repeated in various later sources, including ''[[Star Wars Journal: Captive to Evil]]''<ref name="CTE">''[[Star Wars Journal: Captive to Evil]]''</ref> and "[[The Princess Leia Diaries]]." In the latter source, a ten-year-old Leia wrote in her diary: "Sometimes, a girl just need her mother—especially when you're ten. Why did mine have to die?"<ref name="TPLD">{{Tales|11|The Princess Leia Diaries}}</ref> However, the short story ''Diaries'' was part of the [[Star Wars Tales 11|eleventh issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars Tales]]'' series of comics, the [[canon]]icity of which is ambiguous.<ref name="chee">{{SWBoards|url=message.jspa?messageID=14952461#14944330|thread=Holocron continuity database questions|user=[[Leland Chee|Leland Y Chee]]|date=2006-06-02|time=6:29 PM}}</ref>

By [[2002]], some authors assumed that Bail Organa was single at the time of [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']]. In ''[[Galactic Power Brokers]]'', an article written by [[J.D. Wiker]] for the [[Star Wars Gamer 10|10th issue]] of ''[[Star Wars Gamer]]'', it was stated that Bail Organa was an "eligible bachelor" who "[lacked] interest in courtships" at the beginning of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].<ref name="Gam10">{{GamerCite|10|Galactic Power Brokers}}</ref> The same year, Bail Organa's wife was mistakenly referred to as "Celly Organa" in [[The Official Star Wars Fact File 67|sixty-seventh issue]] of ''[[The Official Star Wars Fact File]]'',<ref name="FF67">{{FactFile|67|ORG 1-2|Bail Organa}}</ref> while Celly Organa was in fact his sister.<ref name="CotJ" /> Eventually, both claims were proved wrong with the release of ''Star Wars Episode III'', which introduced the character of Breha,<ref name="Revenge of the Sith" /> and the novel ''[[Clone Wars Gambit: Siege]]'', which showed that the Organas had already been married for some time by 22 BBY.<ref name="CWGSi" />

"The Kids of ''Star Wars''", an article of the defunct Star Wars Kids segment of [[StarWars.com]], even explicitely referred to Bail Organa as a single parent.<ref name="SWK" /> Additionally, the [[2008]] [[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia|''Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia'']] stated that "With the passing of Queen Breha and the retirement of Bail Organa, their adopted daughter, Princess Leia Organa, became the best-known figure from the royal family in galactic politics." The wording clearly established that Breha died at some point before Bail Organa's senatorial career ended.<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|III|111|Royal House of Alderaan}}</ref>

Eventually, the ''[[2013 Topps Star Wars Illustrated: A New Hope]]'' trading card set released by [[Topps]] in [[2013]] revealed that Breha had indeed survived up until the destruction of Alderaan, thus bringing Leia Organa's line from ''Star Wars 53'' back into canon.<ref name="Topps" />

The Queen received a brief mention in [[Timothy Zahn]]'s novel ''[[Scoundrels]]''. During a chat seance on the "Star Wars Books" Facebook page, Zahn stated that, in his view, Breha was extensively involved with the young Leia's and Winter's upbringing. He also confirmed that the latter's memories of the Queen would "hit [her] particularly hard."<ref name="FBZahn">{{Facebook|username=starwarsbooks|url=starwarsbooks/posts/10151371293428713?comment_id=25439165&offset=50&total_comments=88|name=[[Timothy Zahn]]|date=2013-01-23|quote=I've always thought that Breha had a fair amount to do with Leia's upbringing.|nobackup=1|nolive=1}}</ref>

According to ''[[What's The Story?]]'' author [[Aidan Hennessy]], his [[Databank (original)|Databank]] entry for [[Pello Scrambas]] was supposed to indicate that Breha and Bail's marriage was arranged by [[Jorus C'baoth]] to end the Alderaan Ascendancy Contention. This piece of information, however, was excised from the final Databank entry.<ref name="Blog">{{Blog|QuentinGeorge|3|Pello Scrambas&hellip;uh&hellip;.Scambras&hellip;.whatever - Behind the Scenes}}</ref>

A reference to Breha was made in episode 1.6 of [[Wikipedia:Clerks: The Animated Series|''Clerks: The Animated Series'']]. In it, the characters Randal and Dante discuss why Princess Leia is not Queen of Alderaan, to which Dante says "Her mother had been dead before Alderaan blew up, so wouldn't she be Queen already?" Randal states the whole movie is flawed, like stating for example why do the lightsabers stop where they do. Dante attributes it to the Force, and Randal says "Ah, that's your answer for everything".<ref>{{VisualMediaCite|title=[[Wikipedia:Clerks: The Animated Series|''Clerks: The Animated Series'']]|episode=The Last Episode Ever|director=[[Wikipedia:Steve Loter|Steve Loter]]|prod=[[Wikipedia:View Askew Productions|View Askew Productions]]|year=[[2002]]}}</ref>
